Could you remind me who you are, and what you do here?I've cleared the security pylons - what should I do next?Neural interface is stable... All life signs within normal parameters. You're here, and you're alive! Isn't that wonderful! Hi Player! Are you feeling okay? Is there anything I can help with? Oh, right, sure, of course. Chiara, chief medical officer with the TwilioQuest program. I actually designed the new neural interface through which you are experiencing The Cloud.

It would be a pleasure to meet you in any event, but today it is a particular thrill - I wasn't quite sure this version of the interface was going to work! Did I? Oh, no, I assure you, the neural interface is completely safe.

On an unrelated note - you don't happen to smell fish, do you? I know, what a silly question. Why would you? There's no fish around here!

But if you do start smelling fish, you need to tell me RIGHT AWAY, do you understand? Good? Good. Proceed through the medical bay door into the tech lab. Margaret will want to speak with you next - she'll equip you with a critical tool you'll need while exploring The Cloud. Good luck out there! I'll need you to use basic movement and interaction controls to activate a switch near the exit to the medical bay. If you can do so, we can be confident that your neural interface is configured correctly.

You can move your avatar using the arrow keys, or the W, A, S, and D keys. You can interact with objects - the switch, for instance - using the spacebar. Indeed. You've been selected from thousands of Operators to take command of a prototype Cloud Exploration Vessel we call the Fog Owl. The Owl represents years of research and billions of dollars in cutting edge technology. More importantly, it could finally let us stay one step ahead of the Legacy Systems.

Before we worry about any of that, though, we'll need to check your basic motor functions and ensure you are fit for duty.

all.html:
Operator. I am erecting new firewalls as quickly as I can, but you must retrieve the override codes from Engineer Kubik to abort the Fog Owl's self destruct sequence.

Once you retrieve the codes, use the control panel near the Fog Owl to save the ship and the station. Standing by for query input. I am an advanced artificial intelligence, designed to assist Operators on assignment in The Cloud. When my programming is deemed ready by the TwilioQuest Program, I intend to serve aboard a ship like yours.

I have much to learn about humanity, and I believe direct observation is required to complete my analysis. You presume correctly, and we're excited to finally meet you face to face! Cedric and I have been searching for a long time to find the right leader to take the Fog Owl out on it's first flight, and we think you've got what it takes.

Ready to get on board and take a look around? Operator #00000000000 is credited with the vast majority of commits to my codebase, and has designed much of my training data consumption model and executive functions. Were I a human, I might regard him as a parent. Yeah, of course. Fire away. I'm the director of the TwilioQuest Program. My job is to recruit Operators like you, and support them in any way I can.

These days though, I spend most of my time working on Cedric and his higher order processing functions. I've worked on Cedric's codebase for years now. In many ways, he's like a son to me. At his request, I've tried to teach him about the best parts of humanity: kindness, curiosity, courage...

I'd say he's become an even better human than I am! I'm very proud of his progress, and I think he's ready to serve alongside an Operator. ...

If only you were right. New Operator detected... Cross-referencing classified personnel database... You are the new commander of the Fog Owl, are you not? Hey there! How can we help? Ask, and I shall endeavor to answer them to the best of my ability. Sure - what did you want to talk about? Right? I didn't know if we'd actually use it, but it turns out we do all the time. We can't wait to see what the Owl can do either! Top of the line packet transmission drive, advanced location encryption, and an espresso machine!

The Fog Owl is tough, fast, and stealthy. Once you shake it down and prove that the tech works, we can roll it out to Operators all across The Cloud. Just about. We have a few more calibrations to complete on the starboard TCP ports, but we should have you ready for liftoff inside the hour.

In the meantime, you should check out the ship and meet your crew. They're a good bunch - some of our best. Be sure to lean on them when you need a hand.

On behalf of House Hopper, welcome to Arcane Academy! The amazing thing about APIs is that they’re all about sharing resources and tools.

If code is everywhere, that means that anyone can code. And if anyone can code, that means you can unlock the power of really amazing people – oh, now you’ve got me sounding like I’m in House Turing! We like to test real-life tools, but we’re not just testing; we’re also applying those tools to our API studies. We want to push the bounds of how we wield tools and what they let us do.

To give you a more concrete example, just the other day, I was exploring how to store data with Postman, playing around with Postman parameters that let you create, share, test and document APIs. It blew my mind how helpful the tool was… it also blew a hole through the roof of the greenhouse. But don’t tell my Head of House I said that! House Hopper students are known for their boldness and willingness to try new things. We’re the designated beta testers. We’re not afraid of an API spell still in beta crashing or breaking on us... In fact, the other houses often come to us asking us to break their spells... for R&D purposes, of course.

But seriously, at House Hopper we believe that code is everywhere, and we take it upon ourselves to test out the practical implications of what that means.

Welcome, Operator! You must be off to retrieve your pledge scroll. APIs let you work across mediums to create art, generate beauty, and put good out into the world. Even a simple SMS could be a work of art. Did you know that entire stories have been written in SMS form? Of course! This year House Lovelace is putting on an art show entitled, “Interface Abstractions // Abstract Interfaces” that explores both how API interfaces and abstractions work and how they make us feel. Good APIs are seamless and intuitive, just like a work of art! In fact, you’ll find that many House Lovelace graduates go on to become UX designers and developers. I mean, UX is also an art, don’t you agree? Ah, House Lovelace, house of artists... Here at Arcane Academy we work between expression and technical rigor, where code is functionality but also communication, truth, and expression. Have you ever sat back to observe the elegance of a beautifully executed piece of code?

There’s also an artistry to documentation too, which is our other speciality. In House Lovelace we like to think of API documentation as its own artistic process.

Welcome, Operator! You must be off to retrieve your pledge scroll.

 APIs and their libraries let us share knowledge. We’re putting on a Career Fair for current students, using SDKs and Libraries to set up events, create databases of alumni, and inspire current students with practical applications of APIs after graduation. We truly want to inspire our fellow students to do great things with their skills and knowledge!

Oh, sorry, that wasn’t one sentence… it’s not like I’m in efficiency-loving House von Neumann, though! Every house at the Academy has their own unique traits, and House Turing’s traits are innovation and problem-solving. One way we use those traits is in building a software library, a suite of data and programming code, for our fellow students. We want everyone at Arcane to have access to as many APIs and development kits as possible. You can find the students of House Turing in the labs and garages of the main floor, where we experiment with unsolved API problems. You can also find us training on the field in preparation for codeball season – our mascot is, after all, the tiger! Or you can find us… Well, honestly, you can find us most places at Arcane. We’re involved with practically every club on offer. And if a club - or group or library - doesn’t exist yet, we create them, to solve new problems and bring people together.

I knew you’d have the answer! Thank you so much!

Oh, sure - I'm Mica, your communications officer aboard the Fog Owl. In addition to being fluent in several languages, I can help handle sensitive negotiations or resolve conflicts with anyone we encounter while exploring The Cloud. Hey Operator! Where are we off to today?

The Tower of Infinite Knowledge is the culmination of the life’s work of the figure known as the Librarian. It is always growing, a work in progress, perpetually under construction, for that is the nature of the infinite. But isn’t that the beauty of knowledge and learning? Book 1/4. Chapter 2: The Making of a Librarian

The Librarian was originally programmed to merely collect and preserve data. But as she came to inhabit this program “Librarian,” she developed a bond, with values in a file, with functions in a system, with the ideas and possibilities of something as simple as... data.

Her Tower seeks not only to preserve but to prepare, to equip, to empower travelers with all that knowledge can offer.

Chapter 2: Sources Book 2/4. Chapter 1: Construction

The Tower of Infinite Knowledge was not always a tower. But as the Librarian gathered knowledge according to her programming, it occurred to her that there was also value in sharing it, to help others become developers.

So she first built the idea of the Tower; then she built the Tower itself, including the entire planet from which it extends. Book 2/4. Chapter 1: Construction

The Tower of Infinite Knowledge was not always a tower. But as the Librarian gathered knowledge according to her programming, it occurred to her that there was also value in sharing it. Her knowledge could empower others to become developers!

So she first built the idea of the Tower; then she built the Tower itself, including the entire planet from which it extends. Book 2/4. Chapter 2: Sources

When the Librarian became known as the builder of the Tower, travelers began to bring her knowledge. Archivists came to her with specialized information they wanted her to preserve. The Librarian herself conducted her own research into the needs of developers by launching a program, the New Developer Pain Point Collector, into the Cloud.

How can I help the exploration efforts in the temple? You seem to be alone here - what happened to the rest of the team? Could you remind me who you are, and what you do here? Operator! I was told to expect your arrival. I wish I were better provisioned to welcome you properly, but as you can see, our work here has suffered a bit of a setback. Operator, hello again. Have you discovered anything while exploring the temple? Is that... the Staff of Pythonic Knowledge? Ahahaha I knew it! I knew it was real! This is an incredible find, great work! A cave-in blocked progress into much of the temple, but I managed to clear the entrance to the Initiation Ritual Chamber. This is where new citizens in the ancient City of Python would complete a critical rite of passage.

I've explored the chamber somewhat, but I appear to have triggered some security mechanisms that have barred my progress. Would you be willing to resume my research in this area? Splendid. Though I should note that since the cave-in, I have heard some suspicious noises emanating from the chamber. But I'm sure it's just the wind... in a stagnant, underground temple... I sent the rest of the team home after a cave-in blocked off most of the temple. It happened completely out of the blue, despite our analysis that the temple was structurally sound and safe for exploration. I wouldn't be surprised to learn that the Legacy Systems were behind this somehow.

I am coordinating a salvage team to unblock the rest of the temple, but until then, there is little else for the team to do. Toledo Van Possum, Cloud Archaeologist, and leader of the TwilioQuest research team here at the temple. Though it's not much of a team anymore, is it?

Even so, the opportunity to study the temple is intoxicating. The secrets found inside these walls could fundamentally transform our understanding of the Python programming language. Many years ago, I was a software developer working at a bank in the Netherlands. Banking software, at least to me, was not intrinsically exciting, but uncovering the history was.

Why is this function here? How did this architecture pattern come into use? What were the constraints and trade-offs? These questions started me on a path to trying to understand why the Cloud is the way it is.
